descriptionChirho: Piel declarative sense: to pronounce someone blessed, happy, or fortunate; to call or declare someone's state as one of blessedness. Used of daughters calling Leah blessed (Gen 30:13), of nations calling God's servant blessed (Ps 72:17, Prov 31:28, Song 6:9, Mal 3:12, 15). The Piel form has a declarative-estimative force: not conferring blessing but recognizing and proclaiming it. Multilingual glosses consistently show declarative semantics: arb طَوَّبَ 'to beatify,' deu glücklich preisen, kor 행복하다 하다, spa llamar bienaventurado, hin धन्य कहना.

labelChirho: be called blessed, be deemed happy
descriptionChirho: Pual passive sense: to be called blessed, to be deemed or considered happy. The passive counterpart of the Piel declarative. Attested in Ps 41:2 (the one who considers the poor יְאֻשַּׁר 'shall be called blessed'), and Prov 3:18 (those who hold wisdom מְאֻשָּׁר 'are blessed'). The Pual morphology indicates the subject receives the declaration of blessedness rather than bestowing it. Glosses: eng 'are blessed,' spa 'son bienaventurados,' hin धन्य होगा.

Piel denominative sense from אָשֻׁר 'step': to lead straight, to guide, to direct someone's path. A distinct semantic development from the root's basic meaning 'go straight.' Used of guiding a son in wisdom (Prov 23:19 וְאַשֵּׁר 'and direct'), and of leaders/guides of the people (Isa 3:12, 9:16 מְאַשְּׁרֶיךָ 'your leaders/guides'). The Isaiah passages are notably ironic: the guides lead astray. Glosses show directive semantics: arb قَادَة 'leaders,' eng 'guides,' spa 'guías,' hin अगुवे, kor 이끄는 자들.

Pual passive of the 'guide' sense: to be led or guided by someone. Attested in Isa 9:16 (וּמְאֻשָּׁרָיו 'and those guided by them'), describing the people who follow their misleading leaders. The passive counterpart to the active Piel 'lead/guide.' Distinguished from the Pual 'be called blessed' by context and semantic field: here the subject is being directed along a path, not declared happy. Glosses: eng 'those guided by them,' arb الْمُرْشَدُونَ, kor 인도 받는 자들.

Qal/Piel intransitive sense: to walk straight, go forward, advance on one's way. This is the basic root meaning from which the other senses derive. Attested in Prov 4:14 (תְּאַשֵּׁר 'walk' in the path of the wicked -- a prohibition) and Prov 9:6 (וְאִשְׁרוּ 'and walk' in the way of understanding). The glosses reflect motion semantics: arb اسْلُكُوا 'walk,' eng 'walk,' spa 'avances/caminad,' hin चलो, kor 직행하라 'go straight.'

Piel imperative with forensic nuance: to set right, to correct or reprove an oppressor. Attested in Isa 1:17 (אַשְּׁרוּ חָמוֹץ 'set right the oppressor' or 'reprove the ruthless'). This is a specialized judicial/ethical use, possibly related to the 'guide/direct' sense but applied to correcting wrongdoing. The Arabic أَنصِفُوا 'be fair/just' and Spanish corregid 'correct' support the forensic reading. Some lexicographers relate this to 'lead straight' applied to moral correction.
